description: This file defines the class FinancialValidations, which provides static validation methods for financial calculation inputs such as dates, rates, frequency, basis, prices, yields, etc. It is used internally to ensure input correctness before performing financial computations within the PhpSpreadsheet library.

classes.name: FinancialValidations
classes.description: A utility class providing static methods to validate various financial input parameters such as dates, rates, and numerical values, throwing exceptions when validation fails.

methods.name: validateDate
methods.description: Validates and converts a date input to a float date value using DateTimeExcel helpers.

methods.name: validateSettlementDate
methods.description: Validates and converts a settlement date, internally calling validateDate.

methods.name: validateMaturityDate
methods.description: Validates and converts a maturity date, internally calling validateDate.

methods.name: validateFloat
methods.description: Validates that the input is numeric and converts it to float, throws exception if invalid.

methods.name: validateInt
methods.description: Validates that the input is numeric, converts to integer via floor, throws exception if invalid.

methods.name: validateRate
methods.description: Validates that the rate is a non-negative float, throws exception if negative.

methods.name: validateFrequency
methods.description: Validates that the frequency matches predefined constants (annual, semi-annual, quarterly), throws exception if invalid.

methods.name: validateBasis
methods.description: Validates that the basis is numeric within 0 to 4 inclusive.

methods.name: validatePrice
methods.description: Validates that the price is a non-negative float.

methods.name: validateParValue
methods.description: Validates that the par value is a non-negative float.

methods.name: validateYield
methods.description: Validates that the yield is a non-negative float.

methods.name: validateDiscount
methods.description: Validates that the discount is a positive float (greater than zero).
